column1: # SPDX-License-Identifier: CC0-1.0
# Public Oblivious DoH relays (RFC 9230) that the engine of Advanced's network monitoring may use (ADR 0042, W8). A relay sees the user's address
# but not the question. Every value has its source in sources.tsv; read and measured on 2026-11-20, the project's
# own relay on 2026-11-22 (SOURCE).
# Columns:
#   id             short name, lower case
#   url            the relay's https URL; the relay takes ?targethost=..&targetpath=..
#   ipv4           bootstrap addresses, comma separated
#   ipv6           bootstrap addresses, comma separated, compressed lower-case form
#   operator       the service's operator as it names itself
#   person         the person or body behind it
#   jurisdictions  ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes: the operator's or person's seat, the hosting company's, any CDN's
#   hosting        the hosting networks, as AS numbers
#   cdn            the CDN in front, as AS numbers
#   pins           SPKI SHA-256 pins (sha256/BASE64); none published by any operator
#   note           free text
#   status         '-' for every build; debug for debuggable builds alone, which Advanced's network monitoring
#                  leaves out of a release build's tables (ADR 0055: the project's own relay, until its gates pass)
# '-' means none.
numa
column11: Run by the Numa project on Hetzner Online (DE); the list entry, added by Razvan Dimescu himself, says Falkenstein while the address's RIPE netblock is named CLOUD-NBG1 (Nuremberg); RO is the person's own location on his GitHub profile, no seat of the Numa project is published; no logging statement for the relay on numa.rs; no AAAA record on 2026-11-20

column1: crypto-sx-fastly
column11: A Fastly Compute service maintained by Frank Denis (not Fastly's managed OHTTP Relay product); the host is a CNAME to ecp.map.fastly.net, anycast; FR is the person's own location on his GitHub profile, US is Fastly's seat; the same person maintains the crypto.sx target and curates the DNSCrypt lists; no logging statement for the relay

column1: datapavan
column11: The project's own relay (ADR 0055, proposed): Caddy's configuration in the repository's server/ folder, on datapavan.org's server, a netcup VPS; hosting AS197540, netcup GmbH (Karlsruhe, DE), by RDAP, whose blocks are named DE-NETCUP-20190124 (IPv4) and DE-NETCUP-KVM-VIE (IPv6); DE is the hosting's seat and the server's, TR the operator's seat, where the maintainer resides; it writes no address (ADR 0055, decision 2); debuggable builds only until ADR 0055's gates pass
